manifest.name: Unified downloads
manifest.description: Two independent torrent or Usenet clients with attributable queues, source-specific actions, partial batch results and guest-aware controls.

files.README.md:
# Two download clients

Bind client and optionally secondary to existing Homarr download integrations. Set the two display labels in widget options. The tile renders independent queue queries and errors for each source; a failing or slow client does not hide its sibling. The same normalized native download capabilities support torrent and Usenet backends.

Each per-item action includes the connection name and itemId. The server resolves the current item from that connection, preserving the native client index and never accepting a browser-provided item object. Removal asks for confirmation and keeps downloaded files. Per-source pause/resume work independently. Advanced view and commands can pause or resume all configured clients or selected targets. Every batch reports success/failure per client; failures do not roll back completed external actions. Retry only the failed client when needed.

All control buttons and commands consult useWidgetCapabilities. Guest controls remain disabled until the owner grants the named action and its exact source-qualified input. A narrow example grant is control with {"connection":"secondary","operation":"pause"}. Batch grants explicitly name every target, for example controlBatch with {"connections":["client","secondary"],"operation":"resume"}. Changed bindings/code/resource options invalidate old grants. Native integration action permissions remain authoritative for signed-in users.

Filters, sorting and target selection use shared SDK state across tile/advanced. Composed overview copies these modules and routes them through WidgetScope with the downloads. handler prefix.
